caveats: Requires two threads to call flush() on the same EventDispatcher concurrently: e.g. two task threads whose send() calls both hit buffer_limit (dispatcher.py:192-193), or a send-triggered flush racing the hub-driven _flush_events (consumer.py:624-630) or the reconnect flush (worker/consumer/events.py:50). The deployment model is UNCONFIRMED, so shared-dispatcher multi-threaded use is assumed, not proven.
Whether a twice-published event is observed as a duplicate downstream depends on broker/consumer behaviour outside this tree.
subclaims.reason: flush() snapshots the outbound buffer with list(self._outbound_buffer) at celery/events/dispatcher.py:204 and clears it at dispatcher.py:205, both outside self.mutex, which is only held for the republish loop at dispatcher.py:206-208. Two threads flushing concurrently can each execute line 204 before either executes line 205, so both obtain the full buffer and both republish every event via _publish. The window spans two separate statements, so a thread switch between them needs no switch inside one bytecode region and is reachable under the GIL. No other lock or ordering (start/join, event-loop hand-off) serializes these callers.
